import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 568

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/568](https://www.erdosproblems.com/568)
- [EFRS93] Erdős, P. and Faudree, R. J. and Rousseau, C. C. and Schelp, R. H., Ramsey size linear
  graphs. Combin. Probab. Comput. (1993), 389-399.
-/

namespace Erdos568

/--
Let $G$ be a graph such that $R(G,T_n)\ll n$ for any tree $T_n$ on $n$ vertices and
$R(G,K_n)\ll n^2$. Is it true that, for any $H$ with $m$ edges and no isolated vertices,
$$R(G,H)\ll m?$$

In other words, is $G$ Ramsey size linear?

This problem is #33 in Ramsey Theory in the graphs problem collection.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_568 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      (∃ c₁ > (0 : ℝ), ∀ (n : ℕ) (T : SimpleGraph (Fin n)),
        T.IsTree → (SimpleGraph.graphRamsey G T : ℝ) ≤ c₁ * n) →
      (∃ c₂ > (0 : ℝ), ∀ (n : ℕ),
        (SimpleGraph.graphRamsey G (SimpleGraph.completeGraph (Fin n)) : ℝ) ≤ c₂ * (n : ℝ) ^ 2) →
      G.IsRamseySizeLinear := by
  sorry

end Erdos568

reformulations.difference: The source uses the asymptotic bounds R(G,T_n) ≪ n and R(G,K_n) ≪ n², while Lean requires uniform inequalities for every natural n, including zero.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For each fixed n there are finitely many graphs on Fin n, hence finitely many trees. Any eventual uniform bound extends to all positive n by enlarging its constant to cover the finitely many exceptional graphs; the weights n and n² are at least one there. At n=0 the tree family is empty, and graphRamsey G (completeGraph (Fin 0)) = 0, so neither condition adds an obstruction. The reverse implications are immediate. The equivalence of the entire right-hand side with the eventually-uniform formulation was proved as problem_rhs_iff_eventual in /workspace/review/equivalence.lean; its axioms do not include sorryAx.

sources_consulted: https://www.erdosproblems.com/568 — current status and remarks, read through https://r.jina.ai/https://www.erdosproblems.com/568?review=c90271f0

Erdős, Faudree, Rousseau and Schelp, “Ramsey Size Linear Graphs,” Combinatorics, Probability and Computing 2 (1993), 389–399, DOI 10.1017/S096354830000078X — publisher abstract at https://www.cambridge.org/core/product/identifier/S096354830000078X/type/journal_article
review.notes: The sole theorem faithfully states the source’s question. Constants may depend on G but are uniform over target graphs. The imported definitions correctly use ordinary, non-induced graph Ramsey numbers, positive degree for absence of isolated vertices, and the cardinality of unordered edges. Lean checks in /workspace/review/scratch.lean verified empty and singleton cases, R(K₂,K₂)=2, the bound |V(H)| ≤ 2|E(H)| without isolated vertices, relabelling invariance, and simultaneous satisfiability of both hypotheses for a nonempty G. The current source still records OPEN. The full 1993 paper could not be retrieved: its linked archive PDF returns 404 and the publisher restricts full-text access. Its abstract and both problem-source pages were accessible and sufficient to verify the statement.
